title: SOC 2 trust services evidence
why: SOC 2 is an evidence obligation: the controls can exist and still fail the audit because nobody can show they operated. The packet should ask for the evidence, on a schedule, before the auditor does.

addRequirements.title: Each claimed control has continuous evidence
addRequirements.statement: The repository shall map each claimed control to a machine-checkable artifact whose result is recorded with a timestamp and a revision.
addRequirements.definition: A control is a check that ran, not a paragraph that says it runs.
addRequirements.failurePath: If evidence for a control is missing for the period, the control is reported as unmet rather than assumed satisfied.
acceptance: Given a period with no evidence, when the report is generated, then the control is marked unmet.
Given a passing check, when it runs, then a timestamped record is retained with the revision it ran against.

addRequirements.title: Access is reviewed on a schedule and the review is recorded
addRequirements.statement: When the access-review interval elapses, the application shall produce a list of who holds which privilege for a named reviewer to decide on.
addRequirements.definition: The list of people who can do things is reviewed by a person, on a date, with a decision per row.
addRequirements.failurePath: If the review is overdue, the build reports it and the overdue state is visible rather than implied.
acceptance: Given an overdue review, when the report runs, then it fails and names the date it was due.
Given a completed review, when it is read, then each privilege entry has a decision and a reviewer.
